evidence.claim: The sidecar refuses to pay a transparent recipient, before any proposal or signing
evidence.limits: Sidecar layer only. The LuteGuard (TS) layer refuses the same recipient before any proposal (api test "W1 through the API", recorded as a DENY decision); the forged-ALLOW half of W1 (sidecar refusing even if LuteGuard were bypassed) is this row

evidence.claim: A real shielded payment is delivered in a single pool (Ironwood) and the recipient independently verifies amount and memo
evidence.limits: Funds are a mined fixture (D-007). `verify` uses GetTransaction, which tells the light server this txid interests the caller (PRIVACY.md, pending). Regtest only.

evidence.claim: Mainnet: a payer's own wallet (Zodl) pays a Lute payment request; Lute verifies it by unique address and memo `LUTE:<ref>`, amount, and ≥ 3 confirmations
evidence.limits: The payer wallet chose its own input pool; Lute only sees the Ironwood output it received. `verify` reveals txid interest to zec.rocks (PRIVACY.md). Verified via the sidecar CLI (API not yet deployed).

evidence.claim: Mainnet: a Lute payout to an external shielded address happens only with the owner's Ed25519 approval, in a single pool, with zero transparent
evidence.limits: LuteGuard ordering: LuteGuard returned ALLOW (20/20 checks) on this exact proposal hash, but that evaluation ran seconds *after* execution; the pre-execution ALLOW was on an identical proposal (70ae307d…, hash d621a6a1…) that expired before signing. The API path (`executeAction`) enforces ALLOW-before-execute; to be demonstrated on mainnet. Confirmed: mined at height 3530286, 3 confirmations at tip 3530288 (2026-10-25 16:01 UTC); payout wallet balance afterwards 140000 zat Ironwood = 200000 − 50000 − 10000 fee.

evidence.claim: Mainnet, full path: API → `executeAction` → sidecar proposal → LuteGuard ALLOW recorded before owner authorization → sidecar approve/execute
evidence.limits: Confirmed: mined at 3530306, 4 confirmations at 3530309; payout balance afterwards 110000 zat = 140000 − 20000 − 10000 fee. Closes the E-005 ordering caveat.

evidence.claim: The sidecar spends only with a valid, unused, unexpired owner approval of the exact proposal, and enforces the per-tx and daily caps
evidence.limits: Regtest key is unattended (`--unattended-regtest`), regtest only. Run 2b log was truncated (LOST) and is not cited.

evidence.claim: Mainnet stream: per-second accrual on the server clock, paid out by owner-approved shielded settlements through `executeAction`; accrued, pending and confirmed-paid kept separate; a failed settlement is never counted as paid and becomes due again
evidence.limits: Payer-controlled, not trustless: payouts stop if the payer stops authorizing. Each settlement costs a 10,000 zat fee, so small streams settle rarely. A settlement needs spendable (confirmed) notes; back-to-back settlements must wait for change. The repair of #2 was manual (pre-fix code).

evidence.claim: Streams on regtest through the real API code: per-second accrual, owner-signed settlements via `executeAction` + LuteGuard, pending until mined, paid only when confirmed, recipient verifies with its own keys
evidence.limits: Disposable regtest owner key signs unattended (regtest only). Regtest min confirmations is 1 (mainnet 3).

evidence.claim: An AI agent (MCP/SDK path) pays a metered API from the `agent` wallet only under an owner-signed mandate; LuteGuard denies over-budget spends, and the sidecar independently refuses over-budget, wrong-recipient and unapproved executions even when the API is bypassed
evidence.limits: Regtest key signs unattended (regtest only). Revocation is enforced in the API (LuteGuard GRANT_REVOKED); the sidecar has no revoke and relies on mandate expiry (≤ 48 h). The metered service is an operator-run demo receiving into the `merchant` wallet.

evidence.claim: Mainnet: an AI agent (Claude, through the Lute MCP server) pays a metered API from the `agent` wallet inside an owner-signed mandate, with no per-payment owner signature; past its budget it is denied by LuteGuard with a reason, before the wallet builds anything
evidence.limits: The agent here is Claude driving the MCP server from Claude Code (a Claude Desktop chat client was configured, but the app rewrote its config on quit). The metered API is an operator-run demo receiving into the `merchant` wallet. Agent tokens are bearer tokens: anyone holding one can spend inside the grant until it is revoked or expires.

evidence.claim: Commerce on regtest through the real API code: a checkout is paid by a separate wallet using the ZIP-321 request (address + memo), becomes PAID only when confirmed, gets an Ed25519-signed receipt with no address or item text that verifies (a tampered copy does not), and a partial refund is owner-approved through LuteGuard, capped at what was paid, and verified by the refund recipient
evidence.limits: A first run left the refund SUBMITTED (merchant wallet not synced before the confirmation check); fixed and re-run (this row). Receipts are signed by a key held by the operator (encrypted at rest); they prove what the merchant attests, not more. A refund needs an address from the customer (a shielded payment does not reveal its sender).

evidence.claim: Subscriptions and groups on regtest through the real API code, with real shielded payments from a separate wallet: a subscription is ACTIVE once its period invoice is paid, DUE when the next period starts unpaid, LAPSED after grace; a split bill gives each member their own request and the organizer sees exactly who paid
evidence.limits: Lute never pulls subscription funds (no auto-debit in shielded Zcash): each period is a payment the subscriber makes. Receiving into Lute wallets is the same request path proven on mainnet (E-004).

evidence.claim: Mainnet, on-chain audit: every transaction Lute has made or received is fully shielded on chain (no transparent inputs or outputs, no Sprout, exactly one shielded pool, only the fee leaves the shielded pool); a payment to a transparent address is refused by LuteGuard on mainnet before any proposal; request notes and recipient addresses never appear in plaintext in the database
evidence.limits: `inspect-tx` uses `GetTransaction`, which tells the light server these txids are of interest (they are already public in this repository). The audit covers structure, not timing or network metadata (docs/PRIVATE-PAID-APIS.md).

evidence.claim: Unit tests: recipient inspection (W1, W2, W3-address, W9), single-pool policy (W5, W6, Orchard, multi-step), network params
evidence.limits: Policy unit tests use extracted step facts, not full proposals; the regtest run E-002 exercises the real path

evidence.claim: Payment restrictions hold under concurrency and retries: simultaneous settlements cannot exceed a budget, a retried settlement charges once, a changed recipient is rejected, an expired or revoked grant pays nothing, a payout without approval never executes, a transparent destination is rejected before any proposal
evidence.limits: The API tests use a fake wallet sidecar (the sidecar's own checks are tested separately in Rust, against real SQLite connections on threads). In-process settlement serialization covers one API process; across processes the sidecar's `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` mandate reservation is the backstop (R1 sidecar). Mainnet demonstration of R1/R2 was not run (it would spend the owner's funds).

evidence.claim: Non-custodial (browser-signed) payout: the server holds only a viewing key and cannot spend; the payment is built and proved by the server, checked and signed by the user's signer, and delivered in a single shielded pool
evidence.limits: Regtest only; a mainnet browser-signed payout needs a new account funded by a user. The signer is served by Lute, so the guarantee holds against a passive or compromised server, not an operator who ships different code. The operator still sees payments through the viewing key. The agent wallet stays Lute-held.

evidence.claim: Mainnet: a non-custodial (browser-signed) account receives from Zodl and pays out, with the transaction signed in the user's browser; Lute's server holds no seed or key file for the wallet
evidence.limits: The signer code is served by Lute (guarantee against a passive or compromised server, not an operator shipping different code). The operator still sees payments through the viewing key. Agent wallets and older accounts stay custodial.

evidence.claim: Mainnet: an AI agent (MCP) pays for a useful metered API (document extraction) with a one-time quote, inside an owner-signed mandate, in batched shielded settlements; a payment over the signed per-payment cap is refused
evidence.limits: The first settlement reached the agent as HTTP 500 (web proxy timeout during proving) although it succeeded; fixed (proxyTimeout 180 s); a retry would have reused the same action (idempotency key). 5 of 11 rapid calls were rate-limited. The agent wallet is Lute-held (custodial) by design; the service is operator-run.

evidence.claim: BatchPay: one shielded transaction pays several people from a browser-signed wallet; every line is in the approved hash and checked by the signer; each recipient receives exactly its amount and its own memo; single Ironwood pool
evidence.limits: Regtest only; a mainnet payroll run needs the owner to approve one. A batch shows its number of outputs on chain (4 actions here), not who or how much.

evidence.claim: Mainnet BatchPay: a payroll of two people paid in one shielded transaction, every line in the owner's approval, each person receiving their amount and their own payslip id as memo
evidence.limits: Recipients were the owner's own wallets (a real team would use their addresses). The batch reveals its output count on chain (3 actions), not who or how much. Payslip status turns Paid when the payment's confirmations are recorded (on the next activity refresh).
